Despite this discovery, coupled with the fact that the warhead atop the missile being proven to occasionally detonate it's full nuclear load during uncontrolled explosions, the Strategic Airforce Command determined to cut corners since the missiles cost tens of millions of dollars a piece to make. Instead of scrapping the design or retrofitting them to prevent accidents during takeoff, the SAC instead decrease the 4 megaton warheads to only 2 megatons. This was rationalized by the head of the Strategic Airforce Command's residing officer, who said ironically, "This option is being perused such that in case of a nuclear load being accidentally detonated, the resulting catastrophe will be less catastrophic."

Other fun excepts include: Dozens of live hydrogen bombs burning up on airport tarmacs when a bomber crashed (happened many times), accidentally dropping a live hydrogen bomb off the shore of Savannah Georgia, accidentally dropping various other live nuclear payloads over American soil, unguarded nuclear warheads sitting on airport tarmacs in East Germany, missing nuclear warheads, dozens of nuclear bombs catching fire and burning inside of an armory, nuclear bombers designed to drop bombs with such a blast radius that the bomber would never be able to survive, and doubling the size of a nuclear payload to compensate for a particular ICBM system that had a bad tenancy to miss its target by >20 miles.

This book drew more out loud laughs from me than any other book ever has not because of how any witty writing, but rather because of how completely absurd some accidents were.
